title: Capacity-theft detection, admission-scoring & circuit-breaker for GPU pool exhaustion
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Summary: After the Feb GPU exhaustion event we observed sustained queue amplification from a small number of noisy tenants and a feedback loop between our fast-path admission and autoscaler backoff. This ticket implements a multi-pronged mitigation: (1) lightweight 'capacity-theft' detection to identify tenants whose traffic pattern aggressively consumes burst headroom, (2) admission scoring to prioritize requests by tenant SLA + request characteristics, and (3) a circuit-breaker that trims queues and triggers safe fallbacks when node-level inflight tokens cross thresholds.
impact: The incident caused 3% of requests to experience >2s additional queuing delay for 18 minutes during peak, resulting in elevated client errors and automated retries that amplified the situation. Several high-paying customers reported increased latencies and opened support tickets.
root_cause_summary: Three contributors: (A) a handful of tenants issuing many small concurrency-heavy requests that bypassed our per-tenant smoothing; (B) autoscaler backoff rate that's too conservative, causing slow capacity replenishment; (C) the admission layer lacked tenant-weighted prioritization and a hard ejection mechanism, so queues grew until GPU pools hit eviction thresholds.
decisions: Implement a statistical 'capacity-theft' detector using exponential moving average of token consumption per tenant vs historical baseline (90th percentile). Flag tenants with >3x short-term increase.
Add admission scoring: base score = tenant_priority (SLA tiers) * request_cost_weight + recency_penalty. Admission favors higher score when inflight is constrained.

Circuit-breaker behavior: when node inflight_tokens > 85% of safe_tokens for >20s, begin progressive queue trimming: reject lowest-scoring requests first, then soft-fail to lower-cost model variants, then cut non-critical background requests.

Autoscaler change: introduce short-term emergency scaling signal that prioritizes immediate priming for hotspot pools once capacity-theft is detected, with a conservative cool-down to avoid oscillation.
Telemetry contract: emit 'capacity_theft.flag', 'admission.score', and 'circuit_breaker.state' with tenant_id and pool_id for 30 days of retention.
action_items: A1: Implement capacity-theft detector in admission service (owner: Marco Li) — instrument EMAs, threshold config, and flagging API. (estimate 3)
A2: Add admission-scoring logic and config UI knobs in Console (owner: Priya Rangan) — expose tenant weight and cost model. (estimate 3)
A3: Build node-level circuit-breaker in runtime (owner: Diego Morales) — queue trimming, fallback hookpoints, and safe ejection metrics. (estimate 5)
A4: Autoscaler tweak: emergency priming signal and backoff clocks (owner: Hana Kim) — ensure fast warm-up without thrash. (estimate 3)
A5: End-to-end test harness and chaos tests replaying Feb incident traces (owner: SRE team lead Arun Patel) — create synthetic tenants to validate detection and graceful degradation. (estimate 4)
A6: Update runbook and incident playbook to include capacity-theft escalation (owner: On-call Runbook maintainer). (estimate 1)
A7: Notify top impacted customers with mitigation summary and ETA (owner: Customer Success) — include workaround: set per-request 'priority' header. (estimate 1)
A8: Dashboard: new per-tenant token burn heatmap and alert (owner: Observability team) — Pager rule when a tenant contributes >20% of pool inflight for 10m. (estimate 2)
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring math, integration tests with admission service and runtime fallback hook, system tests that replay captured traffic (sanitized) from the incident. Blue-green rollout in a subset of pools (us-west-2) with synthetic noisy tenants to validate behaviour before global rollout.
rollout_plan: Feature flags: capacity_theft_detection (off by default) -> enroll 10% of pools -> enable admission-scoring in read-only mode (emits scores but doesn't trim) -> enable circuit-breaker soft-fail -> enable hard ejection. Monitor for unintended regressions for 72h at each stage.
monitoring_changes: Emit three new metrics: capacity_theft_count{tenant,pool}, admission_score_distribution{tenant,pool}, circuit_breaker_state{pool}. Create dashboard and set multistep alert: warn at 5% of pools with active breaker, page at 15%.
